newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU confirms ban on South African ostrich imports.
newsitem.headline: EU confirms ban on South African ostrich imports.

text.p: The European Commission has banned the import of ostrich meat and live ostriches from South Africa after an outbreak of Congo fever, a Commission spokesman said on Thursday.
Ostrich meat has gained in popularity in Europe in recent years, due in part to health fears about the possible infection of beef with "mad cow disease".

"For the moment, all imports of ostrich meat from South Africa are banned and we shall also be examining the situation in other African countries," agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely told a news briefing.
The move followed a decision by the EU's standing veterinary committee to apply the safeguard clause to ban the imports.
South Africa said on Thursday it would fight the ban which the Commission said it would re-consider if further research confirmed the disease could not be spread through ostrich meat.
"The ostrich market is highly dependent on the export market," said a South African agriculture department spokesman.

"An official objection will be submitted to the EU requesting the reasons for extending the ban to the total ostrich industry in South Africa, bearing in mind that the recent outbreak was confined to one abattoir only."

The South African Health Department said the ban had been proposed as a precautionary measure, "due to the uncertainty about the safety of ostrich meat for human consumption in the event of an outbreak of Congo fever".
Up to 17 people working at an ostrich abattoir were feared to have contracted the tick-borne fever. One of them has died.

Congo-Crimean haemorrhagic fever is an infectious disease which, like the notorious viral disease Ebola, causes body organs to degenerate with massive internal and some external bleeding. About 30 percent of Congo fever cases are fatal.
Exports from South African ostriches are worth millions of rands a year, and represent some 85 percent of the world market.

Ostrich leather exports exceed 400 million rand ($85 million) each year while an average of 16 million tonnes of ostrich meat valued at 58 million rand is exported annually, according to the agriculture department.
A tick bite caused South Africa's first case of Congo fever in 1981 and sporadic cases have occurred since in rural areas.
